chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi Abu Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Nasawi narrated to us, saying: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Sughadi in Marw narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub ibn al-Hakam al-`Askari and his brother Mu'adh ibn Ya'qub both narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Hanzali narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Asim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays narrated, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Rummani, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Salman al-Farisi (may Allah have mercy on him), in a long hadith which mentions the arrival of the Catholicos to Medina with one hundred Christians after the death of the Prophet (SAWW), and his asking Abu Bakr about issues to which he did not answer, then he was guided to the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) and asked him about them, so he answered him. Among what he asked him was that he said to him: "Inform me about the face of the Lord, the Blessed and Exalted."

Hence, Ali (AS) called for some fire and dry wood and then set fire to it. When it blazed, Ali (AS) asked, "Where is the face of this fire?" The Christian replied, "It has a face from all its sides." Ali (AS) responded, "This fire is supervised and produced, yet its face is not known, while its Creator does not resemble it. And Allah’s is the East and the West, therefore, whither you turn, thither is the Face of Allah. No secret is hidden from our Lord." The hadith is long; we have extracted from it the required passage.

key_terms.الْجَاثْلِيقُ: Catholicos, a high-ranking Christian bishop or patriarch
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ: The East and the West, referring to the directions of creation
key_terms.لَا يُشَبِّهُهَا: Does not resemble it, a key theological concept for divine transcendence
key_terms.مُدْبَرَةٌ مَصْنُوعَةٌ: Supervised and produced/created, indicating a created entity
key_terms.وَجْهُ الرَّبِّ: The face of the Lord, referring to divine presence or attribute

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (AS) explain the 'face of God' using the analogy of fire?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* illustrates the theological debate between the Christian Catholicos and Imam Ali (AS) regarding divine attributes, specifically using the analogy of fire to refute corporeality. By pointing out that fire has no single fixed 'face' but is uniform in its essence, Imam Ali (AS) demonstrates that the Creator is transcendent and unlike His creation, a core tenet of Shia *tawhid*. This incident highlights the Imam’s role as the definitive interpreter of Quranic verses for both Muslims and People of the Book.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 16. Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Farisi Abu Al-Husayn said: Abu Sa`id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nasawi said: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Abd Allah al-Sughadi said in Marw that Muhammad ibn Ya`qub ibn al-Hakam al-`Askari and his brother Mu`adh ibn Ya`qub both said: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Hanzali said: `Abd Allah ibn `Asim said: `Abd alRahman ibn Qays said, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Rummani, on the authority of Zadhan, that Salman al-Farisi (may Allah have mercy on him) related the coming of the Catholicos [al-jathiliq] to Medina with one hundred Christians after the death of the Prophet (SA), and the questions he asked Abu Bakr, and which he was unable to answer. The Catholicos was then sent to the Commander of the Faithful `Ali ibn Abu Talib (AS) and asked him about them; therefore, he answered him. Among the questions he asked him was: “Inform me about the face [wajh] of the Lord, the Blessed and Exalted.”

Hence, `Ali (AS) called for some fire and dry wood and then set fire to it. When it blazed, `Ali (AS) asked, “Where is the face of this fire?” The Christian replied, “It has a face from all sides.” `Ali (AS) responded, “This fire is supervised and produced yet its face is not know, while its Creator does not resemble it. And Allah’s is the East and the West, therefore, whither you turn, thither is the Face of Allah. No secret is hidden from our Lord.” The Compiler of this book says: The tradition is detailed; we have extracted from it the required passage.
